title: Assessing Large Language Models on Islamic Legal Reasoning: Evidence from Inheritance Law Evaluation
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measures the knowledge and reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models in Islamic inheritance law, known as 'ilm al-mawārīth, using multiple-choice questions derived from Islamic legal rulings (fatwas).
findings: There is a significant performance gap between models. Reasoning-focused models like o3 (93.4%) and Gemini 2.5 (90.6%) achieved high accuracy, while open-source Arabic models like ALLaM, Fanar, and LLaMA scored below 50%. The lower-performing models frequently made foundational errors, including misinterpreting legal scenarios, misapplying normative rules, hallucinating fabricated Quranic verses, and basic computational mistakes. Even high-performing models like Gemini occasionally failed on nuanced questions requiring understanding of distinctions between different Islamic legal schools.
